nameOrigin.text: The town is named for Grand Lake, the largest natural body of water in Colorado.

timeline.text: Joseph L. Wescott, credited as the first permanent white settler at Grand Lake, built his cabin on the west shore of the lake.
The Kauffman House was built; the Kauffman family ran it as a hotel until 1946.
The Smith-Eslick Cottage Court, a motor court for automobile tourists, was built in about 1915.
Fall River Road, built from 1913 to 1920, became the first road over the Continental Divide between Estes Park and Grand Lake.
The Grand Lake Area Historical Society bought and restored the Kauffman House.

sites.name: Kauffman House Museum
sites.season: Memorial Day through August; weekends in September

sites.name: Cottage Court Museum
sites.season: Memorial Day through August; Saturdays through September

trails.name: Adams Falls via East Inlet Trail
trails.manager: National Park Service, Rocky Mountain National Park
trails.length: 0.3 mile one way to the Adams Falls viewing area. The East Inlet Trail goes on past Lone Pine Lake, Lake Verna and Spirit Lake to Fourth Lake.
trails.trailhead: East Inlet Trailhead, at the end of West Portal Road near the Town of Grand Lake
trails.season: Open 24 hours a day, all year, weather permitting. Timed entry, a reservation to enter from 9 am to 2 pm that covers East Inlet, ran May 22 to October 12 in 2026.
trails.dogs: Not allowed: pets are prohibited on all park trails, tundra and meadows. Leashed pets (6-foot leash) are allowed only on roads, in parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
trails.fee: Entrance pass required at all hours: $30 a vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7; $15 a person on foot or bike; park annual pass $70. Non-US residents 16 and over add $100 unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

trails.name: Coyote Valley Trail
trails.manager: National Park Service, Rocky Mountain National Park
trails.length: 1 mile on compacted gravel and boardwalk beside the Colorado River, with benches; a 0.1-mile side trail leads to a picnic area
trails.trailhead: Coyote Valley Trailhead, on Trail Ridge Road (US 34) 6 miles north of the Kawuneeche Visitor Center
trails.season: Open 24 hours a day, all year, weather permitting. From late May to mid-October a timed-entry reservation is needed to enter the park’s west side from 9 am to 2 pm.
trails.dogs: Not allowed: pets are prohibited on all park trails, tundra and meadows. Leashed pets (6-foot leash) are allowed only on roads, in parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
trails.fee: Entrance pass required at all hours: $30 a vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7; $15 a person on foot or bike; park annual pass $70. Non-US residents 16 and over add $100 unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

trails.name: Colorado River Trail to Lulu City
trails.manager: National Park Service, Rocky Mountain National Park
trails.length: 3.75 miles one way to Lulu City, an abandoned 1800s mining settlement, the trail’s description says; the park’s trail data gives about 3.4
trails.trailhead: Colorado River Trailhead, 10 miles north of the Kawuneeche Visitor Center on US 34 (Trail Ridge Road), between Timber Creek Campground and Farview Curve
trails.season: Trail Ridge Road is closed to through travel for the season, on the west side at the Colorado River Trailhead. A timed-entry reservation is needed for part of the day from late May to mid-October.
trails.dogs: Not allowed: pets are prohibited on all park trails, tundra and meadows. Leashed pets (6-foot leash) are allowed only on roads, in parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
trails.fee: Entrance pass required at all hours: $30 a vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7; $15 a person on foot or bike; park annual pass $70. Non-US residents 16 and over add $100 unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

trails.name: Arapaho National Recreation Area
trails.manager: Forest Service, Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests, Sulphur Ranger District
trails.size: 35,000 acres with five reservoirs: Lake Granby, Shadow Mountain Reservoir, Monarch Lake, Willow Creek Reservoir and Meadow Creek Reservoir
trails.address: The upper Colorado River valley beside Grand Lake, taking in Lake Granby and Shadow Mountain Reservoir
trails.season: Day use sun-up to sun-down; overnight in campgrounds only. The Stillwater boat ramp is closed for the season; the Sunset Point auxiliary ramp is open 6 am to 6 pm through November 29.
trails.dogs: On a leash in developed campgrounds, picnic and day-use areas and in some wilderness areas, Indian Peaks among them; elsewhere, trails included, under your control at all times.
trails.fee: ANRA pass in fee areas: $5 for 1 day, $10 for 3, $15 for 7, from fee machines or Recreation.gov; $30 annual pass on Recreation.gov only. Interagency passes accepted. No pass needed outside fee areas.
